items.elicits: Commit to integration by parts on x*e^(2x), choose u = x and dv = e^(2x)dx, and carry the reduction through to a correct antiderivative, then name the technique in one phrase.
Factor x^2+x-6 into (x+3)(x-2), split (3x+1)/(x^2+x-6) into partial fractions, solve for the two constants, and integrate each term to a logarithmic antiderivative.
Peel off one sine factor, rewrite the remaining even power of sine with the Pythagorean identity, and complete the u = cos x substitution to a correct antiderivative.
Recognise the x dx numerator as the derivative-linked part of u = 9 - x^2 and carry the substitution through to -sqrt(9 - x^2) + C.

conditions_echo: Declared by the teacher and governing throughout: unsupervised; individual; AI permitted; resources permitted are anything at home, the internet, an AI assistant and a CAS; purpose summative; time not stated; sent home over a weekend after the techniques-of-integration sequence; in the teacher's words, students have practised each technique and these integrands are new to them. The paper's own header reads '40 minutes, no calculator, no notes, closed book', which describes a different administration from the declared one; the declared conditions govern and have not been overruled, so every judgment above follows from the weekend take-home.
reviewer_notes: Novelty holds for all four claims - the teacher states the integrands are new, so nothing here was available to be prepared in this exact form. Claim-targeting also holds: each Part maps cleanly onto one claim (A to K1, B to K2, C to K3, D to K4), with no orphan item and no claim left without an item. Independence is what fails, and it fails uniformly, because 'unsupervised' never qualifies and the permitted resources include the same class of tool that would produce every required output. Because of that, all four claims come back with no independent observation, and delegation is 'yes' in all four cases for reasons specific to each part. Every item is constructed-response, so no guess-rate caveat is triggered anywhere. No component of any claim is absent from the instrument, so Gate 1 fails for all four claims and no missing_evidence is recorded; the limitation is administrative, not a hole in the content. Nothing above describes or implies any change to the assessment, which stands exactly as the teacher uses it.
